highlights.text: ‘You ever think, Whirrun of Bligh, you might take yourself a touch too serious?’ He tipped his head back and stared up into the sky. ‘I’ll laugh when I hear something funny.’
‘Whether Cosca betrayed us or not, whether alive or dead, he is surely in hell now. Just like the rest of us.
‘You have only yourself to blame,’ said Kahdia, calmly. ‘You broke God’s law and ate the flesh of men.’ ‘And of women, and of children, and of everything that breathes.’

‘Did she tell you the time of me kicking you so hard you shit yourself?’ Whirrun’s face took on a contemplative look. ‘She did predict my shitting myself, but that was because of a rancid stew and, anyway, that happened already. Last year, near Uffrith. That is why I have these new trousers.’

Javre’s red hair was a snarled-up tangle, matted with ash, with slime, with food, with things that could not be identified. That should not be identified, lest they offend God to the extent that he felt obliged to end creation.
‘If I have learned one thing in forty years of warfare, it is that doing right … has no end.’

‘What’s peace, Father?’ Bethod blinked down at his older son. Eleven years, and Scale had scarcely seen peace in his lifetime. Moments of it, maybe. Glimpses through a haze of blood. As he struggled to answer, Bethod realised he hardly remembered what peace felt like himself any more.
‘Some men will break a thing just because they can,’ he had whispered. ‘But war must be a leader’s last resort. Fight a war, you’ve lost already.’
‘But Ninefingers is blood-drunk. Murder-proud. Every day he is less your friend, less to be trusted, less a man at all and more an animal. Every day he is less Logen and more the Bloody-Nine.’
